One chart, every number

Miniature Size Chart

Need a number fast? 28mm → 32mm is 114.3%, 32mm → 28mm is 87.5%, and 1:48 → 28mm is 84.1%. The full table below has all 46 conversions I have verified, each with its source and target measurement.

Every figure here comes from the same 175cm human baseline with eyes at 160cm. Gaming labels describe eye level; ratio labels are defined from full height, but I compare eye-level equivalents for every conversion. I print on a Bambu Lab A1 Mini, so the percentages are checked against real parts rather than copied from another chart.

Miniature size chart FAQ

What is a miniature size chart used for?

It gives you the slicer percentage for changing a model from one tabletop scale to another. Find the source scale in the left column, the target scale in the next column, then type the listed percentage into the uniform scale field with X, Y and Z locked.

Why is 28mm to 32mm 114.3%?

Because 32 divided by 28, multiplied by 100, is 114.2857. Both values are eye-level measurements on the same 175cm human baseline, so the ratio is the slicer percentage. The top-of-head variant is about 113.1%.

Which conversions are measured to the top of the head?

Ratio scale names are defined from the top of a 175cm human: 1:35 is 50.0mm to the crown. My conversion percentages compare eye-level equivalents instead, so 1:35 is 45.7mm to the eyes. Gaming scales such as 28mm, 32mm and 35mm are already eye-level labels. The chart shows both baselines so you can see which number I used.

Can I rely on these percentages for every STL?

Use them as the starting point. Sculptors exaggerate proportions and manufacturers drift between ranges. Print one test model, measure it and compare it with a figure you trust before committing to a whole army.

How do I find the scale of an unlabelled STL?

Measure its height in your slicer or with callipers, then use the Miniature Scale Identifier. It compares your measurement with the same baselines used in this chart and hands you a link to the exact conversion.
